questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of the Osculating Circle
questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,4)$ where $t=1,$ given that $‖{r}^{′}(1)‖=3\pi ,$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi {t}^{2}}{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi {t}^{2}}{2})⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(1)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t),$ we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(1)=⟨0,4⟩,$  since the point $P(0,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t),$ ${T}^{′}(1)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(1)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi {t}^{2}}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi {t}^{2}}{2}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi t\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi {t}^{2}}{2}),-\pi t\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi {t}^{2}}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =⟨-\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩=⟨0,-\pi ⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-\pi )^{2}}=\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(1) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{3\pi }{\pi }=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=1$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖}=\frac{1}{\pi }⟨0,-\pi ⟩=⟨0,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1)+R(1)N(1) & =⟨0,4⟩+3⟨0,-1⟩=⟨0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The center is $(0,\pi )$ and the radius $\frac{1}{3}$
The center is $(0,1)$ and the radius $\frac{1}{3}$
The center is $(0,1)$ and the radius $3$
The center is $(0,0)$ and the radius $3$
The center is $(0,-1)$ and the radius $3$

answer_fields.correct_value: The center is $(0,1)$ and the radius $3$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Radius of Curvature Using the Cross Product Formula
questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=0$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,{e}^{-t}⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨1,\,-{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨0,\,{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(0)$ and ${r}^{″}(0)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{3}}{1} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: \sqrt{2}
2\sqrt{2}

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Radius of Curvature Using the Cross Product Formula
questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\pi $ for the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\pi ),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & ={e}^{-t}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & ={e}^{-\pi }⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & ={e}^{-\pi }⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & ={e}^{-\pi }\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{-\pi }\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =2{e}^{-t}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =2{e}^{-\pi }⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =2{e}^{-\pi }⟨0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and ${r}^{″}(\pi )$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi ) & ={e}^{-\pi }⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times 2{e}^{-\pi }⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =2{e}^{-2\pi }\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =2{e}^{-2\pi }\,\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2{e}^{-2\pi }k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖ & =2{e}^{-2\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi ){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{({e}^{-\pi }\sqrt{2})^{3}}{2{e}^{-2\pi }} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}{e}^{-3\pi }}{2{e}^{-2\pi }} \\  & =\sqrt{2}{e}^{-\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: \frac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{\pi }}{2}

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of the Osculating Circle
questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(1,-1)$ where $t=1,$ given that $‖{r}^{′}(1)‖=\sqrt{13},$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}},\,-\frac{3t}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}}⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(1)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(1)=⟨1,-1⟩,$ since the point $P(1,-1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(1)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(1)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3t}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{18t}{\sqrt{{(9{t}^{2}+4)}^{3}}},\,-\frac{12}{\sqrt{{(9{t}^{2}+4)}^{3}}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{{(9{t}^{2}+4)}^{3}}}⟨-3t,\,-2⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{{(9({1}^{2})+4)}^{3}}}⟨-3(1),-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{6}{13\sqrt{13}}⟨-3,-2⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{6}{13\sqrt{13}}\cdot \sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{13\sqrt{13}}\cdot \sqrt{13} \\  & =\frac{6}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(1) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{(\frac{6}{13})} \\  & =\frac{13\sqrt{13}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=1$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}⟨-3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1)+R(1)N(1) & =⟨1,-1⟩+\frac{13\sqrt{13}}{6}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}⟨-3,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1⟩+\frac{13}{6}⟨-3,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1⟩+⟨-\frac{13}{2},-\frac{13}{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{11}{2},-\frac{16}{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The center is $⟨-\frac{7}{2},\frac{11}{3}⟩$ and the radius is $\frac{\sqrt{13}}{3}$
The center is $⟨\frac{15}{2},-\frac{11}{3}⟩$ and the radius is $\frac{13\sqrt{13}}{6}$
The center is $⟨-\frac{1}{2},\frac{7}{3}⟩$ and the radius is $\frac{13}{6}$
The center is $⟨\frac{13}{2},-\frac{16}{3}⟩$ and the radius is $\frac{\sqrt{13}}{3}$
The center is $⟨-\frac{11}{2},-\frac{16}{3}⟩$ and the radius is $\frac{13\sqrt{13}}{6}$

answer_fields.correct_value: The center is $⟨-\frac{11}{2},-\frac{16}{3}⟩$ and the radius is $\frac{13\sqrt{13}}{6}$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of the Osculating Circle
questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,1)$ where $t=0,$ given that $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖=\sqrt{2},$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(0)=⟨0,1⟩,$ since the point $P(0,1)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(0)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,-1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=0$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)+R(0)N(0) & =⟨0,1⟩+\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1⟩+⟨-1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The center is $⟨0,1⟩$ and the radius is $\sqrt{2}$
The center is $⟨-1,0⟩$ and the radius is $2$
The center is $⟨-1,0⟩$ and the radius is $\sqrt{2}$
The center is $⟨1,1⟩$ and the radius is $\sqrt{2}$
The center is $⟨0,-1⟩$ and the radius is $2$

answer_fields.correct_value: The center is $⟨-1,0⟩$ and the radius is $\sqrt{2}$
